draft.title: Commercial electrolytic cells
card: Industrial electrolytic cells are designed to make a product cheaply and safely on a large scale. The electrodes and electrolyte are chosen to suit the product wanted.
Electrodes must conduct electricity and not react in unwanted ways. Inert electrodes such as graphite or titanium are often used. Some electrodes are made from the metal being refined.
The electrolyte must contain the ions needed to make the product. Some cells use a molten electrolyte. Others use an aqueous solution.
Products are removed as they form. This keeps the products apart so they cannot react with each other, and it allows the cell to run continuously.
draft.remember: Commercial cells match electrodes and electrolyte to the product and remove it as it forms.

a.q: Why do industrial cells remove products as they form?
opts: To stop the products reacting together and let the cell run on
To make the reaction spontaneous without a power supply
To raise the voltage the power supply must provide
To change the electrolyte into a different substance
a.why: Removing products keeps them from reacting with each other, such as a gas reacting with a metal, and lets production continue. It does not make the reaction spontaneous, because the power supply is still needed.
a.clue: Think about what could happen if products stayed mixed together.

b.q: A company designs a cell to make chlorine gas from salt solution. Why would it choose graphite or titanium electrodes?
opts: They conduct electricity and are inert, so they do not react
They react with chlorine to make the process cheaper
They dissolve into the solution to replace the ions used
They stop the solution from conducting electricity
b.why: Inert electrodes carry current without being used up or changing the products. Electrodes that reacted with chlorine would be damaged and would contaminate the product.
b.clue: An electrode should carry current but not take part.
